subject: Log Provenance & Export Orchestration — packaging options and timeline
messages:
From: James Harrow <james.harrow@umbra-bank.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: regtech-ops@umbra-bank.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request: compliant log export packaging and verification options

Dylan,

Thanks for taking this. Umbra's compliance team needs a definitive description of how Redwood can deliver audit-log exports that preserve provenance and support independent verification. Key asks:

- Signed manifests or checksums (preferably detached signatures) per export slice.
- Incremental snapshot semantics (we want daily deltas + occasional full snapshots).
- Chain-of-custody metadata so we can demonstrate no tampering during transit.
- Options for encryption at rest/in-transit and customer-managed key integration.
- Expected timelines for a 90-day rolling export for an initial data set (~1TB compressed).

We have a hard compliance review on 2026-11-12 and would like a recommended delivery schedule and a sample manifest/schema to show auditors. Can you also outline the verification steps the auditor would run (hash checks, signature verification, ordering guarantees)?

Regards,
James Harrow
Head of RegTech Ops | Umbra Bank
regtech-ops@umbra-bank.com
+1 415 555 0172

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: James Harrow <james.harrow@umbra-bank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: compliant log export packaging and verification options

James,

Appreciate the clarity — attaching a short options summary (export_options_summary.pdf) that outlines 3 supported packaging patterns and timelines. High-level answers inline: 

- Signed manifests: we support a per-bundle JSON manifest that includes file-level SHA-256, byte ranges, sequence tokens, and a detached PKCS#7 signature. We can optionally sign with a Redwood key and/or provide the manifest unsigned for you to re-sign with a customer-managed key (KMIP/HSM).

- Incremental snapshots: we offer daily incremental bundles (rdw-incr-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz) plus weekly full snapshots. Bundles include a sequence range header to support gap detection and replays.

- Chain-of-custody: each export record is tagged with server-side timestamp, export node ID, and export job id. The manifest includes a verifiable provenance chain (parent snapshot id + delta id). We can mint a tamper-evident audit token (signed statement) for each transfer.

- Encryption & KMS: S3-delivery options include AES-256 server-side, SSE-KMS with customer-managed keys, and client-side envelope encryption. TLS 1.3 for transit.

- Timeline for 1TB (compressed): initial full snapshot + manifest generation: 24–36 hours from authorized request; daily increments: ~2–4 hours (depending on peak load and retention policy). We can prioritize and parallelize initial harvest for a faster window under a dedicated job.

Attached: export_options_summary.pdf (overview). I've looped in Marissa for scheduling and Karthik for security specifics. If helpful, I can send a manifest template and a sample verification checklist.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Confirm desired packaging pattern (daily deltas vs. hourly streaming + weekly full).
2) Decide on signature model (Redwood-signed, customer-signed, or both).
3) Agree on delivery mechanism (S3 presigned, SFTP, secure FedEx for offline media).
4) Book a 30–45m runbook review before 2026-11-08 so we can finalize materials for your audit.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — that helps. Two follow-ups: 

1) For incremental bundles we need deterministic ordering guarantees for events within each bundle (to allow timeline reconstruction). Do your sequence tokens provide global ordering within a tenant, or are they per-shard? How should auditors interpret them?

2) For very-large restores (e.g., reconstructing 30 days), what is your estimated end-to-end verification time (hash + signature checks) if the auditor runs locally against the delivered tarballs? Any tooling you provide to accelerate verification?

Also please send the manifest template and the auditor checklist so we can validate the wording with legal.

Regards,
James

Subject: Re: Request: compliant log export packaging and verification options

James —

Following our call today, attaching the manifest template and the verification checklist you requested. Quick summary of items we agreed and the runbook: 

1) Packaging: daily increments + weekly full snapshots. File naming: rdw-full-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz and rdw-incr-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz. Each bundle contains a manifest.json, payload files (.ndjson or .parquet as requested), and a signature.sig (PKCS#7 detached).

2) Ordering & tokens: sequence_token is a monotonically increasing integer scoped to the tenant (global ordering per-tenant). Each event record includes sequence_token and recorded_at timestamp. The manifest includes start_sequence and end_sequence; auditors can validate contiguous ranges. Shard ids are provided for performance details but do not affect ordering claims.

3) Verification tooling: we include a lightweight verification script (verify_export.py) that performs: file hash verification, PKCS#7 signature check (using either Redwood cert or a provided public key), sequence continuity check, and a summary report. For 30 days (~30 daily increments + 4 weekly fulls) against 1TB data, we estimate verification on auditor hardware (8 vCPU, 32GB RAM, NVMe) to take ~2–4 hours; parallelizable across bundles. We'll provide a Dockerized verifier to standardize runtime.

4) Chain-of-custody & manifest fields (included in template): export_job_id, node_id, generated_at, start_sequence, end_sequence, file_checksums, encryption_metadata, signature_info, parent_snapshot_id.

5) Delivery & keys: S3 presigned links with SSE-KMS (customer key) is the default. For air-gapped handoff, we can stage onto encrypted removable media and ship via approved carrier (additional lead time).

6) Timeline: schedule initial full within 24–36 hours after signed authorization; daily increments thereafter. We will run a dry-run export within 48 hours of sign-off to validate tooling and timelines for auditors.

Attachments: provenance_manifest_template.json (text/json), delivery_sops.md (text/markdown). Also shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-umbra-export-spec (contains verifier Dockerfile and sample outputs).

Please confirm acceptance of the packaging pattern and whether you want Redwood to perform the signature with our key or if Umbra will supply a public key to sign manifests post-delivery. Once you confirm, Marissa will schedule the dry-run and Karthik and I will circulate the runbook steps.

Best,
Dylan
